title: The normalized Roos comparison respects integer shifts
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ with exact countable products [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the unbounded derived categories of $\mathcal A$ and of its strict positive-integer inverse towers [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Let $\rho_X:\mathsf C(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim X$ be precisely the normalized Roos comparison of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], where $\mathsf C(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod X_n\to\prod X_n)[-1]$ and $R\lim$ is computed by K-injective tower resolutions and termwise inverse limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit, def-pur-kinjective-complex]. In coordinates $\mathsf C(X)^i=(\prod X_n)^{i-1}\oplus(\prod X_n)^i$ with differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-dy-(1-s)x,dx)$, for every $r\in\mathbf Z$ the map
$$\sigma^C_{X,r}:\mathsf C(X[r])\longrightarrow\mathsf C(X)[r],\qquad(y,x)\longmapsto((-1)^r y,x)$$
is a natural chain isomorphism. These maps give the coherent termwise Roos shift. Let $\sigma^{\lim}_{X,r}:R\lim(X[r])\to(R\lim X)[r]$ be the shift comparison represented by shifting a K-injective tower resolution $X\to I$ to $X[r]\to I[r]$ and identifying $\lim I[r]=(\lim I)[r]$. Then
$$\sigma^{\lim}_{X,r}\circ\rho_{X[r]}=\rho_X[r]\circ\sigma^C_{X,r}.$$
The normalization is retained: the inclusion $\lim I\to\mathsf C(I)$ with coordinates $(0,z)$ commutes with these shift maps. The equality is natural for all derived strict-tower morphisms, independent of the resolution and coherent for $r=0$ and addition of integers. In particular the equation applies after any natural strict-tower comparison commuting with the termwise shifts.

proof.text: Write $P_X=\prod_nX_n$, $h_X=1-s_X$ and $a=(-1)^r$. Termwise products identify $P_{X[r]}=P_X[r]$ and $h_{X[r]}=h_X[r]$. By the cochain convention and the explicit strict Roos coordinates, the differential on $\mathsf C(X[r])$ is $(y,x)\mapsto(-a d y-h_Xx,a d x)$, whereas on $\mathsf C(X)[r]$ it is $(y,x)\mapsto(-a d y-a h_Xx,a d x)$. Applying $(y,x)\mapsto(a y,x)$ before or after these differentials gives $(-d y-a h_Xx,a d x)$ in either order, since $a^2=1$. Thus the displayed map is a chain map and its inverse is the same coordinate map.

source.place: Tag 011G, definition-shift-cochain; signed calculation using derived.tex Tag 014E, definition-cone

proof.text: For a strict tower map $f:X\to Y$, the map $\mathsf C(f)$ is diagonal with the product of the $f_n$ on both coordinates. It commutes with $\operatorname{diag}((-1)^r,1)$ because each $f_n$ is additive. This proves naturality before localization. Under the usual termwise identifications of iterated shifts, the composite $\sigma^C_{X,r}[s]\circ\sigma^C_{X[r],s}$ multiplies the first coordinate by $(-1)^s(-1)^r=(-1)^{r+s}$ and fixes the second. Hence it is $\sigma^C_{X,r+s}$, and $\sigma^C_{X,0}=1$.

source.place: Tag 011G, definition-shift-cochain and the immediately following shift-addition identities; derived.tex Tag 014E

proof.text: Use the K-injective tower representative of [lem-pur-injective-tower-roos-shifts]: choose $q:X\to I$ with $I$ K-injective and with injective tower objects in each degree; its termwise inverse limit represents $R\lim X$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift] in the abelian category $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ to see that $q[r]:X[r]\to I[r]$ is again a K-injective resolution. Its terms are the terms of $I$ reindexed, so they are still injective tower objects. The same representative theorem identifies $\lambda_{I,r}:\lim I[r]\to(\lim I)[r]$ as the termwise total-limit shift. Its components are identities on compatible limit tuples.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, first paragraph; derived.tex Tag 070H, definition-K-injective and the following shift observation

proof.text: Let $j_I:\lim I\to\mathsf C(I)$ and $j_{I[r]}:\lim I[r]\to\mathsf C(I[r])$ be the normalized inclusions. By [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] both are quasi-isomorphisms, and in these representatives $\rho_X=j_I^{-1}\circ\mathsf C(q)$ and $\rho_{X[r]}=j_{I[r]}^{-1}\circ\mathsf C(q[r])$, with all maps now read in the derived category. The inclusion has coordinates $(0,z)$, so the calculation $\sigma^C_{I,r}(0,z)=(0,z)$ gives the actual chain-map identity $\sigma^C_{I,r}\circ j_{I[r]}=j_I[r]\circ\lambda_{I,r}$. Thus the normalization, including its sign, is retained.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, kernel inclusion in the short exact sequence; coordinate refinement using derived.tex Tag 014E

proof.text:
Invert the localized inclusions in the preceding identity to get $\lambda_{I,r}\circ j_{I[r]}^{-1}=j_I[r]^{-1}\circ\sigma^C_{I,r}$. Naturality from step 2 applied to $q$ gives $\sigma^C_{I,r}\circ\mathsf C(q[r])=\mathsf C(q)[r]\circ\sigma^C_{X,r}$. Substitution into the normalized resolution formulas now gives
$$\begin{aligned}\sigma^{\lim}_{X,r}\circ\rho_{X[r]}&=\lambda_{I,r}\circ j_{I[r]}^{-1}\circ\mathsf C(q[r])\\&=j_I[r]^{-1}\circ\mathsf C(q)[r]\circ\sigma^C_{X,r}\\&=\rho_X[r]\circ\sigma^C_{X,r}.\end{aligned}$$
This compares the specified maps, rather than choosing an isomorphism of the two cones.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, normalized kernel-cone comparison; agent shift refinement

proof.text: The comparison theorem makes $\mathsf C$ and $\rho$ functorial on the derived tower category. The strict-map naturality identity in step 2 therefore holds also for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms, by multiplying that identity by their images on both sides, and hence for every localized morphism. Resolution choices do not change the total-limit shift: given another K-injective resolution $q':X\to J$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents $(Qq')(Qq)^{-1}$ by a tower chain map $v:I\to J$ with $vq$ homotopic to $q'$. It is a quasi-isomorphism, hence a homotopy equivalence by the same cited statement. Termwise limit preserves its homotopies: the limit of a tower homotopy $H$ satisfies $d(\lim H)+(\lim H)d=\lim(dH+Hd)$ after every limit projection. Moreover $\lambda_{J,r}\circ\lim(v[r])=(\lim v)[r]\circ\lambda_{I,r}$ after every projection, because both components are $v_n^{i+r}$. These equalities identify the shift from $J$ with the one from $I$, even when $J$ has no injective terms. Finally step 5 gives $\sigma^{\lim}_{X,r}=\rho_X[r]\circ\sigma^C_{X,r}\circ\rho_{X[r]}^{-1}$. The right side is resolution independent and natural for all derived tower morphisms; so is the stated equality.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, (1) implies (3); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941 and agent signed naturality refinement

proof.text: For $r=0$ the last conjugation formula gives the identity. For $r,s\in\mathbf Z$, substitute it twice into $\sigma^{\lim}_{X,r}[s]\circ\sigma^{\lim}_{X[r],s}$. The adjacent $\rho_{X[r]}^{-1}[s]$ and $\rho_{X[r]}[s]$ cancel, leaving $\rho_X[r+s]\circ(\sigma^C_{X,r}[s]\circ\sigma^C_{X[r],s})\circ\rho_{X[r+s]}^{-1}=\sigma^{\lim}_{X,r+s}$ by step 2. Thus the equality respects shift coherence. For a natural strict-tower comparison $b:X\to Y$ commuting with the termwise shifts, its two product maps give the diagonal $\mathsf C(b)$ from step 2. Combining its naturality square with that of $\rho$ composes the proved square with $b$ on either side. This proves the last assertion with the same normalized maps.
